rows.question: What is the role of SAP IAS (Identity Authentication) and IPS (Identity Provisioning) when deploying SAP Cloud SAP Cloud IAG?
rows.answerText:
SAP IAS (Identity Authentication) plays a crucial role in authenticating users accessing SAP Cloud IAG (Identity Access Governance) by providing Single Sign-On (SSO) capabilities and enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) policies. It acts as the identity provider, validating user credentials and issuing tokens for secure access to cloud applications.

On the other hand, SAP IPS (Identity Provisioning) is responsible for synchronizing user identities and executing provisioning writes. It supports the Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) process by managing user lifecycle events, ensuring that access rights are updated accordingly. While IAS handles authentication, IPS focuses on provisioning and identity synchronization, allowing IAG to govern access requests, manage roles, and enforce compliance effectively. To validate this setup, I would ensure that users can successfully authenticate through IAS and that their access rights are accurately reflected in IAG after provisioning actions are executed by IPS.
